messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-12345 fired for service=redwood-inference-serving region=us-west-2 reason=GPU_VMEM_BACKPRESSURE pool=gpu-pool-prod-3 severity=high

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert -> INC-12345 created, responders: @raj.s (primary oncall), @dana (secondary)

maria.k: seeing a stream of `cuMemAlloc` failures and slab allocation errors on node gpunode-prod-3, repeated OOMs across multiple models. cpu ok, but vmem keeps creeping.

samuel: logs from node: 
```
[2024-02-14T22:12:03Z] cudart: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory (err=2)
[2024-02-14T22:12:03Z] runtime: kvcache eviction storm: evicted 12mb -> 0 reclaim
[2024-02-14T22:12:04Z] allocator: failed to reserve 1.2GB contiguous region
```

samuel: also seeing a lot of KV cache fragmentation — prefix cache spikes followed by sustained vmem usage. not immediate CUDA driver reset but allocations start failing.

raj.s: acked on PD, jumping in. I've paged infra to check node-level fragmentation and host swap settings. Sam, can you check recent deploys? any quantization/profile changes?

maria.k: there's a scheduled heavy batching job from internal analytics hitting the cluster around the same time — looks like a misrouted batch that used production GPU pool instead of dedicated analytics pool.

jordan: confirmed — deployment job id: batch-2024-02-14-21:55 mis-targeted to `gpu-pool-prod-3` due to a selector bug.

raj.s: action plan: 1) stop the offending batch job 2) drain gpunode-prod-3 from new allocations 3) kick rolling restart of aio-serv on that node to clear fragmented caches 4) enable temporary fallback routing to smaller model variant for prod traffic

samuel: running commands now: 
```
# cordon + drain new workloads
kubectl cordon gpunode-prod-3
kubectl drain gpunode-prod-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
# cancel batch job
kubectl delete job batch-2024-02-14-21:55
```

pagerduty-bot: INC-12345 acknowledged by raj.s at 2024-02-14T22:14:10Z

dana: oncall standby, pulling up runbook: /runbooks/gpu-vmem-backpressure.md. If drain doesn't free enough, we'll evict large KV caches and scale out temporarily.

maria.k: customer impact: we see a spike in 500/503s for a subset of keys routed to the node — BetaCorp and three other high-traffic tenants saw degraded tail latency and errors. Postgres ingestion unaffected.

raj.s: notifying CS and sending initial status: "Investigating GPU memory pressure affecting generation endpoints in us-west-2. Mitigations in progress; some customers experiencing 5xxs. Will update in 15m." @maria.k please paste minimal incident note for shared channel.

maria.k: posted to #customer-impact: "Investigating GPU memory pressure in us-west-2 affecting text-gen endpoints. Some customers may see errors or degraded latency. Mitigations underway."

samuel: drain completed, restarting serving processes on gpunode-prod-3. Restart logs show KV cache reclaimed partially, but heap fragmentation still present.

jordan: scaling up pool by 2 nodes to reduce pressure and enable routing fallback. patching routing rules to move 30% of traffic to model-small variants.

raj.s: executing routing change (route id r-204) to divert traffic now.

incident-bot: route-change applied r-204: 30% -> model-small, 70% -> model-default; expected latency impact +20ms for diverted requests.

maria.k: customers BetaCorp reported client retries reduced errors after reroute. Monitoring shows error rate falling from 12% -> 1.8% over 6 minutes.

samuel: still seeing sporadic cuMemAlloc failures but not system-wide. likely fragmentation plus residual KV cache growth. I'll run targeted eviction: `redis-kvcache evict --node gpunode-prod-3 --age 300s --prefix-regex ".*conv.*"`

dana: I'm taking over active pagerduty rotation. Raj, can you document actions so far and handoff? I'll monitor for 30 minutes and coordinate postmortem.

raj.s: handoff: stopped misrouted batch job, cordoned/drained node, restarted serving, applied routing fallback to smaller model, scaled pool +2, evicted hot KV prefixes. Current status: degraded -> improving, error rate trending down, no new PD pages. PD INC-12345 remains acknowledged and assigned to dana for monitoring.

pagerduty-bot: INC-12345 reassigned to dana at 2024-02-14T22:22:01Z

dana: thanks. I'll keep watch and kick off postmortem draft after stabilizing. Notes for postmortem: tighten admission controls for batch jobs, add selector validation for analytics clusters, add auto-eviction policy for KV fragmentation, consider autoscale based on vmem pressure metric.

maria.k: also recommend adding an alert that correlates sustained kv_cache_evictions with cuMemAlloc errors to avoid noisy single-metric triggers.

dana: agreed. I'll also escalate to infra for a potential kernel allocator tuning if repeated. For now, continuing to monitor. Will update channel when incident is closed. :eyes:
